These regulations have been instrumental in ensuring the structural integrity of buildings during earthquakes.​ 2️⃣Regular Structural Assessments: Developers like Raimon Land Public Company Limited (RML) have conducted swift structural inspections across their developments, affirming compliance with top-tier seismic safety standards. Such proactive assessments help identify and address potential vulnerabilities before disasters occur. ​ 3️⃣Public Awareness and Preparedness: Thailand has invested in public education campaigns to raise awareness about earthquake preparedness. These initiatives have equipped citizens with the knowledge to respond effectively during seismic events, reducing panic and potential injuries.​ While the overall resilience was commendable, the collapse of the high-rise under construction highlights the need for continuous evaluation and enhancement of construction practices. Experts have emphasized the importance of rigorous enforcement of building codes and the incorporation of advanced engineering techniques to further bolster structural resilience. ​ Thailand's experience during the March 2025 earthquake underscores the critical role of stringent building codes, regular structural assessments, and public preparedness in mitigating earthquake damage. By learning from recent events and continually improving its infrastructure and response strategies, Thailand can further enhance its resilience against future seismic activities.

🇲🇲Myanmar is reeling following the huge earthquake which hit the country on Friday, 28 March. The 7.7 magnitude tremor was felt elsewhere, including in Thailand and south-west China. More than 2,700 people have died and more than 4,500 have been injured, say the leaders of Myanmar's military government. Those figures are expected to rise. In Thailand, at least 21 people lost their lives.🏥 WHAT CAUSED THE EARTHQUAKE? 🌎 The earth's upper layer is split into different sections, called tectonic plates, which are all moving constantly. Some move alongside each other, whilst others are above and below each other. It is this movement that causes earthquakes and volcanoes. Myanmar is considered to be one of the most geologically "active" areas in the world because it sits on top of the convergence of four of these tectonic plates - the Eurasian plate, the Indian plate, the Sunda plate and the Burma microplate. The Himalayas were formed by the Indian plate colliding with the Eurasian plate, and the 2004 Tsunami as a result of the Indian plate moving beneath the Burma microplate. Dr Rebecca Bell, a reader in tectonics at Imperial College London, said that to accommodate all of this motion, faults - cracks in the rock - form which allow tectonic plates to "slither" sideways. There is a major fault called the Sagaing fault, which cuts right through Myanmar north to south and is more than 1,200km (746 miles) long. Early data suggests that the movement that caused Friday's 7.7-magnitude earthquake was a "strike-slip" - where two blocks move horizontally along each other. As the plates move past each other, they can become stuck, building friction until it is suddenly released and the earth shifts, causing an earthquake. Myanmar's Devastating Earthquake: International Cooperation and Diplomatic Advantages for the Military Regime Myanmar, April 2, 2025 — Following Myanmar's deadliest natural disaster, the position of junta leader Min Aung Hlaing has been strengthened, as diplomatic channels that had been closed for over a year have been reopened after the earthquake. Following the 7.7 magnitude earthquake last Friday, which killed over 2,700 people, Min Aung Hlaing has found a new diplomatic opportunity amidst Myanmar’s crisis. After the earthquake, Min Aung Hlaing was preparing to attend a regional summit in Thailand, where he was contacting leaders of other countries by phone to meet with them. While it is still unclear whether Min Aung Hlaing will attend the BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) summit, the disaster has helped end his diplomatic isolation. Analyst Angshuman Chowdhury says, "This is an opportunity for Myanmar’s regional powers, such as India, China, and Russia, who would want to increase their influence." He further stated, "Min Aung Hlaing can use this opportunity to solidify his leadership as indispensable in Myanmar." In the past week, Min Aung Hlaing has spoken with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, resulting in international aid starting to flow. Prior to this, due to the pressure of the war and defeats faced by the junta government, Min Aung Hlaing had become isolated on the international stage. Analysts suggest that this earthquake could complicate Myanmar’s battlefield and make it harder to maintain support among local populations, intensifying the resistance struggle. Meanwhile, Myanmar’s junta government is trying to seize the opportunity to receive aid, but it is facing obstacles in reaching opposition groups and the general public. China, India, Russia, and Southeast Asian countries have sent aid to Myanmar, but military operations by the junta continue. Additionally, if Min Aung Hlaing participates in the BIMSTEC summit, his international legitimacy could increase further, especially as his relationship with India strengthens. India has already quickly sent aid following the earthquake. Min Aung Hlaing may also get an opportunity to meet with regional leaders, including Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Thai politician Thaksin Shinawatra. However, Thailand is taking a cautious stance as it shares a long border with Myanmar and faces significant economic and security risks. Analyst Thitinan Pongsudhirak states, "Thailand has to work very carefully because they have a lot at stake in their relationship with Myanmar." This situation has opened up a new diplomatic opportunity for Myanmar’s junta government, although internal conflicts and violence within the country continue.

A study by Chinese seismologists, published just days before a deadly magnitude 7.9 earthquake hit Myanmar on March 28, 2025, warns of a rising risk of major earthquakes in China and surrounding regions. Led by Zhu Hongbin of the Beijing Earthquake Agency, the research links seismic activity to fluctuations in Earth’s rotational speed, measured as changes in the length of a day (LOD). Analyzing 150 years of data, the team identified six “active periods” of earthquakes in the region, with the current phase focusing on the Bayan Har block near the Tibetan Plateau. They suggest that tectonic stress is shifting northeast, raising risks in areas like Sichuan, Yunnan, and the Himalayas. The Myanmar quake, which killed over 3,000, aligns with their predictions, but some experts, like Gao Mengtan, argue that global seismic activity in 2025 remains below average, casting doubt on claims of a new “shaking mode.” Recent smaller tremors in Tibet, Xinjiang, and Guangdong, plus a magnitude 7.3 quake near Tonga, have heightened attention on the study’s findings. https://t.co/nV6WHalH7u

Japan Dispatches JSDF Transport Aircraft to Myanmar for Earthquake Relief Efforts – 7 April 2025 Asahi Shimbun, 7 April 2025. Japan has decided to dispatch Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF, 自衛隊) units to Myanmar as part of an international emergency assistance operation to support victims of the recent earthquake. The mission will involve transporting medical supplies and equipment via JSDF aircraft. Defense Minister Gen Nakatani (中谷元) is expected to make a formal announcement soon. Details of the Relief Operation On 6 April 2025, multiple government officials confirmed the JSDF’s deployment, marking the first international emergency aid operation since the Turkey earthquake in 2023. A JSDF survey team entered Myanmar on 3 April 2025 to gather information on the disaster and assess local needs. Initially, debris removal activities were considered, but concerns over security in the region led to a decision to limit the JSDF deployment to approximately 20 personnel. On 7 April 2025, Nakatani officially announced the deployment of a JSDF C-130 transport aircraft from Komaki Air Base (小牧基地), Aichi Prefecture, scheduled for departure on 8 April 2025. The mission will transport approximately 2.5 tons of medical supplies and equipment essential for ongoing relief operations in the Mandalay region. The aircraft is expected to reach Mandalay International Airport on the morning of 9 April 2025. The decision to dispatch JSDF units comes amid heightened concerns about growing Chinese and Russian influence in Myanmar, as both nations have sent their own aid to the disaster-hit region. Japan, which does not officially recognize Myanmar’s military government, approached the deployment with caution, coordinating efforts between the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. According to Nakatani, the JSDF maintained readiness to dispatch aircraft from the initial stage of the disaster. This marks the first international emergency assistance operation overseen by the newly established Joint Operations Command (統合作戦司令部). The JSDF established a local coordination office in Myanmar to facilitate information gathering and communication. Coordination with International Partners The Quad nations—Japan, the United States, Australia, and India—held vice-ministerial-level telephone discussions and issued a joint statement calling for a safe environment conducive to providing humanitarian assistance. They emphasized the importance of ceasefires and extensions to facilitate relief operations. Japan’s relief efforts are being carried out in collaboration with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), which has already deployed a medical team to Mandalay consisting of 32 medical professionals, including doctors and nurses. The supplies transported by the C-130 aircraft will directly support this team’s operations. Future Implications Japan’s decision to dispatch the JSDF to Myanmar reflects its strategic concerns over Chinese and Russian influence in the region. The mission demonstrates Japan’s commitment to providing humanitarian assistance while carefully navigating complex political and security considerations. Japan Dispatches Air Self-Defense Force Transport Plane to Deliver Medical Supplies to Myanmar Following Earthquake - 8 April 2025 NHK, 8 April 2025. On 8 April 2025, a Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF, 航空自衛隊) C-130 transport aircraft departed from Komaki Air Base (小牧基地) in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, carrying approximately two tons of medical supplies, testing kits, and tents. This mission aims to support Japanese medical teams operating in Myanmar following a major 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck central Myanmar on 28 March 2025. Deployment and Personnel The Japanese government deployed a medical team consisting of over 30 individuals, including doctors and nurses, as part of the International Emergency Assistance Team. Approximately 20 JASDF personnel are participating in the relief mission, demonstrating Japan’s commitment to providing timely humanitarian assistance in response to large-scale natural disasters. Departure and Arrival Details The C-130 transport aircraft departed from Komaki Air Base at around 2:30 PM on 8 April 2025. Its destination is Mandalay International Airport, located in Myanmar’s second-largest city of Mandalay, which experienced extensive damage from the earthquake. The aircraft is expected to arrive on the morning of 9 April 2025. Supplies Delivered to the Affected Area The aircraft is transporting approximately two tons of essential medical supplies, including testing kits and tents, to aid Japanese medical teams and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA, 国際協力機構) teams operating on the ground. These supplies are critical for the continuation of relief efforts, ensuring that medical support can be sustained in the disaster-affected region. Operational Command and Coordination The newly established Joint Operations Command (統合作戦司令部) is overseeing the mission, reflecting enhanced coordination within the Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF). The operation was initiated following a request from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, highlighting interagency collaboration in providing international emergency assistance. Commercial Flight Limitations and Previous Deployments Due to the suspension of commercial flights in the affected region, the use of a JASDF transport aircraft is essential for ensuring the timely and reliable delivery of medical supplies. The United Nations has faced scrutiny for its humanitarian efforts in conflict zones, with some questioning its impartiality. Meanwhile, the NUG has called for a temporary ceasefire to facilitate relief, though clashes persist. International aid, including search-and-rescue teams from countries like China, India, and Thailand, has been welcomed for saving lives trapped under rubble. Critics argue that UN assistance appears to prioritize junta-controlled areas, potentially neglecting civilians in NUG-held regions like parts of Sagaing, where the earthquake’s impact was severe. The junta is diverting aid to support its personnel and loyalists, such as setting up tents for military staff, rather than prioritizing displaced civilians or earthquake victims. The UN’s role in Myanmar should be impartial, ensuring aid reaches all affected populations, regardless of who controls the territory. Operating in a conflict zone is challenging, and the safety of UN staff is a valid concern. However, if security risks prevent equitable aid delivery, the UN must find ways to work with both governments to reach civilians in opposition areas or reconsider its approach entirely. Myanmar’s people are enduring not only the aftermath of a natural disaster but also the ongoing horrors of war, with airstrikes and displacement affecting both junta- and NUG-controlled regions. We urge the UN to uphold its humanitarian principles by distributing aid fairly to all earthquake victims and conflict-affected communities. Japan Ends Emergency Medical Airlift to Myanmar Following Earthquake Relief Operations – 22 April 2025 Japan Ministry of Defense, 22 April 2025 On 22 April 2025, Minister of Defense Nakatani (中谷) announced the conclusion of the Japan Self-Defense Forces’ (JSDF, 自衛隊) emergency airlift mission to Myanmar, initiated in response to a 28 March earthquake centered in central Myanmar. The humanitarian operation involved the deployment of a C-130 transport aircraft from Komaki Air Base (小牧基地), which delivered critical medical supplies to Mandalay on 9 April for use by Japanese emergency medical teams operating in the disaster-stricken region. This marks the first such mission under the command structure of the newly established Joint Operations Command (統合作戦司令部). Humanitarian Relief Mission On 7 April, Defense Minister Nakatani issued an order to the Joint Operations Commander to commence international emergency assistance operations using JSDF air transport assets. In execution of this directive, a C-130 aircraft departed Komaki Air Base on 8 April and arrived at Mandalay International Airport the next day. The aircraft successfully handed over humanitarian medical supplies to Japan’s dispatched international emergency response teams. After the delivery, one C-130 remained on standby in Japan, while personnel at the on-site JSDF coordination office continued monitoring the situation. The operation was deemed complete on 22 April following a comprehensive assessment indicating a significant decrease in disaster-related casualties in the affected region. Political and Diplomatic Context Defense Minister Nakatani personally welcomed the returning JSDF aircraft at Komaki, commending the personnel’s dedication. He relayed gratitude expressed by Myanmar civilians, emphasizing the symbolic importance of Japan’s prompt aid. The mission holds strategic importance as the first international relief action conducted by the JSDF under the newly structured Joint Operations Command, established to enhance operational integration and response agility. Minister Nakatani affirmed Japan’s intent to continue exploring humanitarian aid options to directly support Myanmar’s recovery even after the conclusion of the JSDF’s emergency mission. U.S.-Japan Relations & Defense Dialogue In response to a separate question on trade-security linkage, Minister Nakatani reaffirmed Japan’s position that economic matters, such as tariff negotiations, should be considered independently of defense and security cooperation. He noted that this stance aligns with Prime Minister Ishiba’s recent remarks. Referring to his recent defense meeting with U.S. Secretary of Defense Hegseth on 30 March, the minister emphasized Japan’s commitment to enhancing deterrence and response capabilities within the U.S.-Japan alliance. Nakatani also welcomed the newly appointed U.S. Ambassador to Japan, Mr. Glass, and expressed eagerness to deepen strategic dialogue. Domestic Issues: Military Symbolism and Base Construction Minister Nakatani addressed recent controversy surrounding the interpretation of a farewell poem by General Ushijima, which was included in a speech by the first commander of the Provisional 1st Combined Group (臨時第１混成群). He clarified that his interpretation highlighted a message of peace rooted in historical commitment to Okinawa’s welfare, while affirming that civilian control remains paramount. Additionally, Nakatani provided updates on the halted construction of JSDF accommodation facilities in Nishinoomote City, Kagoshima Prefecture. Work was suspended in November 2024 due to underground obstructions. Discussions with local authorities to resolve the matter are ongoing.
